title: Split-weight mutation during staged rollout caused transient mixed-serve and capacity surge; suppressive quarantine playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Post-incident ticket: during a staged A/B model rollout we observed a transient mixed-serve window where traffic was split inconsistently between variants and a concurrent autoscaler reaction caused a capacity surge. This ticket captures the incident summary, timeline, root cause analysis, and a prioritized set of mitigation and long-term action items to prevent recurrence and reduce blast radius of similar rollouts.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-17 14:03 UTC a partial metadata fanout combined with a weight mutation race in the rollout controller produced inconsistent route translations across proxies. A small fraction of nodes served both old and new variants simultaneously, producing higher-than-expected backend saturation and triggering autoscaler burst capacity. The combination caused elevated latencies for ~22 minutes and a small fraction of failed requests for some customers using heavy-token workloads.
timeline: 2026-02-17 13:57 UTC - Canary release initiated: promo weight target 10% -> 30% phased ramp
2026-02-17 14:02 UTC - Orchestrator applied staged weight update to subset of shardsets
2026-02-17 14:03 UTC - Metadata fanout lag (replica A) created inconsistent route epoch on ~8% of serving nodes
2026-02-17 14:04 UTC - Proxy route translator computed weights using stale predicate leading to split-weight mutation on affected nodes
2026-02-17 14:05 UTC - Autoscaler observed increased per-node CPU and launched burst capacity; some nodes started serving mixed variants while new shards were being provisioned
2026-02-17 14:25 UTC - Monitoring alert: latency P95 spike > 2x baseline; automated canary-safety gate fired but failed to fully quiesce due to partial pin state
2026-02-17 14:30 UTC - Emergency mitigation: operator triggered safe-quarantine which pinned old variant and drained affected nodes
2026-02-17 14:45 UTC - Traffic returned to expected distribution; post-incident triage started
impact: Elevated latencies for 22 minutes across multiple customers, error rate increase of up to 1.7% for token-heavy generation requests, temporary extra cloud cost from burst autoscaling (~$1.2k estimated). No data exfiltration or model misprediction concerns were observed.
root_cause: A race between rollout controller weight updates and the metadata fanout led to inconsistent route epochs on a subset of serving nodes. The proxy's route translation merged stale predicates and new weights producing a mutated split that allowed mixed-serve. The autoscaler reacted to increased per-node load before the rollout gate fully stabilized, amplifying the impact.
mitigations: Immediate: manual pin of old variant on affected route to stop mixed-serve
Short-term: increase rollout gating delay to wait for metadata fanout quiescence before applying weight increments
Short-term: add a canary-healthcheck that verifies uniform route epoch across >= 95% nodes before traffic ramp
Long-term: implement route checksum verification on proxy startup and before applying weight deltas
Long-term: make rollout controller updates idempotent and attach monotonic update IDs so out-of-order apply is ignored
Long-term: add autoscaler-awareness to rollout controller (suppress ramp while autoscaler is in mid-provisioning)
Observability: emit rollout-diff events and a per-route 'epoch-consistency' metric surfaced in Console
action_items: ADD-001: Implement route-epoch checksum in proxy and fail-fast on checksum mismatch (owner: Marco Li, estimate: 3) - due 2026-03-12
ADD-002: Rollout controller: attach monotonic update ID to each weight mutation and reject older IDs on apply (owner: Dana Rodriguez, estimate: 5) - due 2026-03-19
ADD-003: Orchestrator: introduce 'fanout-quiesce' step - wait for fanout ACKs from >90% replicas before committing next weight step (owner: Priya Menon, estimate: 3) - due 2026-03-12
ADD-004: Autoscaler integration: temporarily pause weight ramps when horizontal scaling events are in-flight (owner: Samir Patel, estimate: 5) - due 2026-04-02
ADD-005: Safety gate: add a pre-ramp canary check that compares route translation hash across nodes and blocks ramp if mismatch detected (owner: Marco Li, estimate: 2) - due 2026-03-05
ADD-006: Playbook: publish 'quarantine and pin' runbook and run tabletop with SRE/Oncall (owner: Aisha Kapoor, estimate: 1) - due 2026-02-28
ADD-007: Cost control: add billing alert for anomalous autoscaler-burst costs tied to rollouts (owner: FinanceIntegrations team, estimate: 2) - due 2026-03-15
ADD-008: Testing: add a chaos test in integration that simulates metadata fanout lag during staged rollouts (owner: QA, estimate: 3) - due 2026-04-09
